name: og-34-chemical-heredity-and-selection
title: Chemical Heredity and Selection
gate_reason: Gate D (reproduction and heredity), second half: heritable variation and selection. Using study 33's division, the test is whether a chemical difference inherited by a daughter protocell causes reproducible differences in survival or reproduction - whether there is heritable variation selection can act on. Inheritance is carried by NETWORK COMPOSITION partitioned at division first (⚑3 Option B, compositional / GARD-style, tied to the og-06 heredity rescope and its vasas-2010 evolvability caveat); template copying is tracked as a budgeted follow-up (og-34a), not a buried caveat. Crucially, fitness is GROUNDED in the real study-32/33 coupling: the inherited composition sets membrane retention via the study-32 MD-informed relation (longer chain -> higher retention), which raises the standing pool and so the division rate (study 33) = fitness - so selection acts on a trait with a real mechanistic fitness consequence through the merged machinery, not a toy fitness function. The gate half is met only if, at input fluxes held equal to a no-inheritance control (daughters reset to a common composition), an inherited difference produces a reproducible parent-offspring fitness difference above that control AND a population under selection shifts composition measurably rather than drifting. Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalytic (A2 refuted). RESULT: there IS selectable chemical heredity on the compositional-inheritance first cut (verdict qualified) - a reproducible parent-offspring fitness correlation and a population shift, both permutation-significant vs the no-inheritance null; the vasas-2010 caveat was tested and the population shifts rather than drifts.
claim: A daughter-inherited chemical difference produces a reproducible fitness difference that selection acts on, shown against a matched no-inheritance control (daughters reset to a common composition) at equal feeds. Heredity is carried by inherited network composition (Option B), and fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling - composition sets membrane retention (study 32), which sets the standing pool and division rate (study 33) - so selection acts on a trait with a genuine mechanistic fitness consequence. Across seeds and generations, an inherited composition difference yields a parent-offspring fitness correlation far above the no-inheritance control, and the inheriting population shifts composition toward higher retention while the control drifts. The vasas-2010 evolvability caveat was TESTED (a declared, not tuned, heritable variance) and the population shifts rather than drifts - so compositional inheritance carries enough selectable variance here. Verdict qualified: compositional inheritance (Option B); template copying (Option A, og-34a) is the higher-fidelity follow-up. The metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network (not autocatalytic), so selection acts on the inherited composition of a carbon-fixing network, not a self-amplifying one.
question: Does a chemical difference inherited by a daughter protocell cause reproducible differences in survival or reproduction - is there heritable variation selection can act on?
hypothesis: Compartments carrying different inherited network compositions show reproducible, heritable fitness differences under the vent feed, so a population shifts composition under selection rather than drifting. If inherited composition produces no reproducible fitness difference above a no-inheritance control, or a population does not shift measurably, no selectable heredity is claimed.
objective: Run a multi-compartment population of study-33 dividing protocells under selection on an inherited network-composition trait whose fitness is grounded in the study-32/33 retention -> division-rate coupling; measure the parent-offspring fitness correlation and whether a population under selection shifts composition - against a matched no-inheritance control (daughters reset to a common composition) at input fluxes held equal, reporting no-selectable-difference honestly if that is the result. Instantiates the og-06 heredity rescope.

model_approach.prose: Study 34 asks whether the protocell has something for selection to act on. Daughters inherit the parent's network composition; the question is whether that inherited difference reproducibly changes how well a daughter reproduces - a parent-offspring fitness correlation - and whether a population under the vent feed then shifts composition rather than drifting. What makes the test meaningful rather than a toy is that fitness is grounded in the real merged machinery: composition sets membrane retention (study 32), which sets the standing pool and the division rate (study 33). The hard rules are the campaign's evidence standard: input fluxes are held equal to a no-inheritance control (daughters reset to a common composition), so any heritable fitness difference is a margin over that control; significance is a dependency-free permutation test. Crucially the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat is TESTED, not assumed - compositional inheritance may not carry enough variance for selection, and whether the population actually shifts is the readout. Inheritance is Option B (network composition); template copying is tracked as a budgeted follow-up (og-34a).

decision_test: At input fluxes held equal to a no-inheritance control (daughters reset to a common composition), an inherited network-composition difference must produce a reproducible parent-offspring fitness difference above that control (permutation-significant) AND a population under selection must shift composition measurably rather than drift. Failing either (no reproducible fitness difference, or drift only) is a reported negative - including the vasas-2010 outcome that compositional inheritance lacks selectable variance - not tuned (evidence standard #6, #8).

findings.statement: There IS selectable chemical heredity (not the vasas-2010 null). Across 8 seeds x 40 generations at equal feeds, an inherited network-composition difference yields a reproducible parent-offspring fitness correlation (mean +0.949) far above the matched no-inheritance control (-0.018; permutation p=0.0001). Fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling (composition -> membrane retention -> standing pool -> division rate), so the correlation reflects a genuine mechanistic fitness consequence. Guardrail: selection acts on the inherited composition of the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis.

The inheriting population shifts composition measurably under selection (mean shift +0.551 toward higher-retention / longer-chain composition) while the matched no-inheritance control drifts (-0.004; permutation p=0.0002). Selection acts because both heritable variation and a reproducible fitness difference are present - the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat was tested (declared heritable variance sigma=0.03, not tuned) and the population shifts rather than drifts.

Heredity is carried by inherited NETWORK COMPOSITION (Option B, compositional / GARD-style), with the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat TESTED, not assumed - compositional inheritance carried enough selectable variance here for selection to act. Template copying (Option A, og-34a) is the higher-fidelity follow-on that would re-test selectable heredity under a copying mechanism, especially where compositional inheritance might prove too low-variance in other regimes.

limitations: Inheritance mechanism = Option B, chosen as the first cut: network composition partitioned at division (compositional / GARD-style), with the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat (compositional inheritance may lack selectable variance) TESTED against the no-inheritance control using a declared, not tuned, heritable variance (sigma=0.03) - not assumed away. Option A (template-copying inheritance, a higher-fidelity copying mechanism) is tracked as a chemistry follow-up (og-34a) in discovery_implications, not a hidden caveat.

Fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling (inherited composition -> study-32 MD-informed membrane retention [endpoints 0.333/0.661] -> standing pool -> study-33 division rate), so selection acts on a real mechanistic consequence rather than a toy function; the composition->retention map carries the study-32 MD-informed (not PMF-resolved) caveat. Selection is modelled as Wright-Fisher reproduction in proportion to fitness over a finite population (n=80) and generations (40), with significance from a dependency-free permutation test (PyMC is the richer stat, not installed here). A drift-only / no-shift outcome would have been an accepted negative, reported not tuned. The enclosed metabolism is the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis (A2 refuted under vent conditions).

resolved_uncertainties: Inheritance-mechanism scope, resolved by Eran (via coordinator): chosen = Option B - inherited NETWORK COMPOSITION partitioned at division (compositional / GARD-style). Tractable, tied to the og-06 heredity rescope and the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat (which the study tests rather than assumes), and its fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling. Deferred = Option A - template copying (a higher-fidelity copying mechanism); tracked as the follow-up below, not buried as a limitation.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether template-copying inheritance (Option A) would change the selectable-heredity verdict in regimes where compositional inheritance proves too low-variance - i.e. whether the vasas-2010 variance limitation bites under different fitness landscapes, resolved only by a copying mechanism.

followup_study_proposals.title: Template-copying inheritance (higher-fidelity heredity)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Study 34 takes selectable heredity on an Option-B first cut (inherited network composition), and the population shifts under selection with the vasas-2010 caveat tested. Option A - template-copying inheritance - is the gold-standard test of whether selectable heredity holds under a higher-fidelity copying mechanism, especially in regimes where compositional inheritance would prove too low-variance.
followup_study_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: A copied template (sequence-like carrier) partitioned at division, giving higher-fidelity heritable variation than compositional inheritance, replacing network-composition inheritance.
followup_study_proposals.compute_budget_note: Requires template-copying chemistry (reaction-rule-generation, to-build); scheduled when that wrapper exists.
